title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after police stopped their car on July 23 on Calle Duran. A Flock Safety camera mistakenly read their license plate, which ended in 2, as 7, matching a stolen vehicle from Rio Rancho. Officers handcuffed Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister, identified as DD, and placed them in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, but the girl was still handcuffed and detained.

The lawsuits, filed January 3, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also filed a similar case in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was forced to kneel after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. No next steps are stated beyond the pending lawsuits.
